application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client library built on the fetch API, providing a $fetch wrapper with automatic JSON handling, retries, timeouts, hooks, and normalized errors, with Node.js and global-fetch entry points.
application.purpose: Simplify making HTTP requests in JavaScript/TypeScript applications by wrapping fetch with sensible defaults, response parsing, retry logic, and consistent error reporting.

domains.name: HTTP Client
domains.description: Core request construction, sending, and response handling via fetch.

domains.name: Request Resilience
domains.description: Retry policies, retry delays, and timeout/abort handling for requests.

domains.name: Error Normalization
domains.description: Creation of enriched FetchError objects carrying request, response, and status details.

domains.name: Hooks and Configuration
domains.description: Lifecycle hooks (onRequest, onResponse, etc.) and default option merging via create().

domains.name: Runtime Adaptation
domains.description: Selecting fetch, Headers, and AbortController implementations for global or Node.js environments.

terminology.meaning: The main exported callable that performs a request and returns the parsed response body.
A variant of $fetch that returns the full response object including the parsed _data.
Normalized error type carrying request, options, response, and status information.
HTTP statuses (e.g. 408, 429, 500, 503) that trigger automatic retries.
HTTP methods that carry a request body (PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE), used to decide retry defaults and body handling.
User-supplied callbacks run at request, response, and error stages.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Factory that builds the configured $fetch client, including the raw request pipeline (option resolution, body serialization, timeout, response parsing, hooks) and the create() method for derived clients.
Error pipeline that decides whether to retry a failed or error-status request and otherwise throws a normalized FetchError.
Builds a FetchError with a descriptive message combining method, URL, status, and underlying error, and exposes request/response/status properties.
Checks whether an HTTP method carries a request body, affecting body handling and default retry count.
Determines whether a request body should be automatically JSON-encoded.
Chooses how to parse a response (json, text, or blob) based on the Content-Type header.
Merges per-request options with client defaults, combining query/params and headers.
Combines default headers with request-specific headers into a single Headers object.
Invokes one or more lifecycle hook functions in sequence with the current request context.
Provides a fetch implementation for Node.js, optionally enabling keep-alive agents via the FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable.
Manual development script that issues a sample request to a failing endpoint to exercise error handling.
Example script showing typed JSON fetching of a repository record from a public API.
Test helper that aborts a request via AbortController and verifies that retry with abort does not continue.

applicationFacts: The library exports $fetch, ofetch, and create-based derived clients built by createFetch.
The deterministic graph shows createFetch calling resolveFetchOptions, callHooks, isPayloadMethod, isJSONSerializable, detectResponseType, and onError.
onError calls isPayloadMethod and createFetchError, and retries requests for retry-eligible status codes or non-abort errors.
Default retry status codes are 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 unless overridden.
Response bodies are parsed with destr for JSON responses unless parseResponse is provided.
Timeouts are implemented by aborting a controller after the configured timeout.
The package is built with unbuild with entries src/index and src/node, and externalizes undici.
The graph contains a self-recursive CALLS relation on createFetch, reflecting the retry path that calls $fetchRaw.
unknowns: The graph lists createFetch as calling itself, but the source shows the retry path calls $fetchRaw; the mapping between these inner functions and the graph's entity IDs is not fully clear.
The graph does not include $fetchRaw or the inner functions as separate entities, so their CALLS relationships cannot be confirmed.
The purpose of the test helper abortHandle is inferred from its name and body and may not reflect the full test intent.
Whether the playground and example scripts are intended for production use is not stated.
